s1.syndrome_frame: obstructive sleep disorder with upper airway obstruction
salient_findings: cystic mass at the base of the tongue
key_facts: 20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base

raw.syndrome_frame: obstructive sleep disorder with upper airway obstruction
salient_findings: cystic mass at the base of the tongue
key_facts: 20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: cystic mass at the base of the tongue

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid
shortlist.why_kept: cystic mass in the midline of the tongue base

shortlist.label: Ranula
shortlist.why_kept: cystic lesion in the tongue base causing airway obstruction

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: well-defined cystic lesion in the tongue base

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: cystic mass with potential for airway obstruction

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base, as shown on contrast CT of the neck, is consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst, which is a common congenital anomaly that can cause obstructive sleep apnea due to its location and potential to compress the airway.

rejected.label: Lingual thyroid
rejected.why: Although it can also cause airway obstruction, lingual thyroid typically presents with a more solid mass and is often associated with thyroid dysfunction, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Ranula
rejected.why: Ranula is a type of mucous cyst that occurs in the floor of the mouth, not typically at the base of the tongue, and is less likely to cause significant airway obstruction.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Dermoid cysts can occur in the head and neck region but are less common in the tongue base and may not typically present with the same degree of airway obstruction as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are rare tumors that can contain multiple tissue types and can occur in the head and neck, but they are less likely to present as a well-defined cystic lesion in the tongue base causing obstructive sleep apnea.
